Course 1: The Creation of Man (Death through Adam)

The Creation of Adam In Genesis 2:7, God forms Adam from the dust of the earth and breathes life into him. Adam becomes a living being, created in God's image (Genesis 1:26-27). This creation narrative establishes humanity's unique relationship with God.

Genesis 1:26-27 ~ Then God said, “Let Us make man in Our image, according to Our likeness; and let them rule over the fish of the sea and over the birds of the sky and over the cattle and over all the earth, and over every creeping thing that creeps on the earth.” God created man in His own image, in the image of God He created him; male and female He created them.

The fall of Adam

Adam's disobedience in the Garden of Eden (Genesis 3) introduces sin and death into the world. Through Adam's actions, humanity becomes separated from God, leading to spiritual and physical death (Romans 5:12-19).

The Consequences of Adam's Sin

1. Separation from God: Sin creates a rift between humanity and God.

2. Death and suffering: Sin introduces death, suffering, and decay into the world.

3. Human nature: Adam's sin affects human nature, leading to a tendency toward sin and rebellion.

The Effects of the Fall God promised that if they disobeyed, Adam and Eve would “Surely die” (Genesis 2:17) a truth which Satan denied (Genesis 3:45). God, of course, had not lied, and His words came to pass. In order to understand the depth of the tragedy, we need to understand what death is. Death always speaks of separation. From that day we clearly see the following:

• Man is separated from God. He died spiritually. He instantly became aware of his own failures, his shame, and his nakedness.

• Man is separated from Man. We see the beginning of a breakdown in the trust between man and wife (Genesis 3:16) and in the next chapter the breakdown between brothers with jealousy, anger and murder.
• Man is separated from nature. From that day work was hard and often unpleasant (Genesis 3:17-19).

• Man is separated from the Tree of Life. Man was then removed from the garden and denied access to the Tree of Life. In other words, he would no longer be “immortal”. From that day he began to die physically.

The Connection to Jesus Christ

The story of Adam serves as a backdrop for understanding Jesus Christ's role in redemption. Through Jesus, humanity can be restored to a right relationship with God (Romans 5:12-21).

Scripture: Genesis 13 (creation narrative), Romans 5:12-21 (Adam and Christ comparison), 1 Corinthians 15:21-22 (death through Adam, life through Christ).

Restoration through Jesus Christ

"The first Adam brought death, but the last Adam, Jesus Christ, brings life." Through faith in Jesus, believers can experience:

1. New life: Spiritual rebirth and transformation (2 Corinthians 5:17).

2. Reconciliation: Restoration of the relationship between God and humanity (Romans 5:10).

3. Victory over sin: Empowerment to overcome sin and live a life pleasing to God (Romans 6:1-23).



Summation: As understanding the creation narrative and the fall of Adam helps us appreciate the significance of Jesus Christ's redemptive work. Through Adam, we see the consequences of sin, but through Jesus, we see the gift of salvation and new life. May we embrace this gift and live as children of God, empowered by the Holy Spirit.







Course 2: New Birth of life through Christ (Dead to sin alive in Christ)

Understanding the New Birth

Through faith in Jesus Christ, believers experience a new birth, becoming dead to sin and alive in Christ (2 Corinthians 5:17, Romans 6:1-11). This transformation is a powerful work of God, enabling believers to live a life pleasing to Him.

Dead to Sin

1. Freedom from sin's power: Believers are no longer slaves to sin but are freed to live for God (Romans 6:6-14).

2. Crucified with Christ: Believers' old selves were crucified with Christ, putting an end to sin's dominion (Romans 6:6), Galatians 2:20).

Alive in Christ

1. New life : Believers have been given new life in Christ, empowered to live a life pleasing to God (Romans 6:4-5,11).

2. Union with Christ: Believers are united with Christ, sharing in His resurrection life (Colossians 3:14, Ephesians 2:56).

(2 Corinthians 5:17) "Therefore, if anyone is in Christ, the new creation has come: The old has gone, the new is here!"

Romans 6:1-11: Explains the believer's death to sin and new life in Christ.

Galatians 2:20: "I have been crucified with Christ and I no longer live, but Christ lives in me."

Colossians 3:14: Encourages believers to seek heavenly things, united with Christ.

Summation: The new birth in Christ is a powerful transformation, freeing believers from sin's power and enabling them to live a life pleasing to God. Through faith in Jesus, believers are dead to sin and alive in Christ, empowered to live victoriously.





Course 3: The Blood of Jesus

Introduction: what is blood? Blood is life, it's spiritual. (Lev.17:11) For the life of the flesh is in the blood: and I have given it to you upon the altar to make atonement for your souls: for it is the blood that makes an atonement for the soul. The Blood is a connection between a man and God; The life of every fleshly creature is in the blood. The effects of any blood depends on the value, which is purity and magnitude of what it carries in it.

(Exod.12:13) "And the blood shall be to you for a token upon the houses where ye are: and when I see the blood, I will pass over you, and the plague shall not be upon you to destroy you, when I smite the land of Egypt."

(Rev.12:11) And they overcame him by the blood of the Lamb, and by the word of their testimony; and they loved not their lives unto the death.

The "blood of Jesus “refers to the sacrificial death and atoning work of Jesus on behalf of humanity , offering forgiveness of sins and redemption through faith.it refers to the profound and transformative power of Jesus' sacrifice , offering forgiveness, cleansing, and reconciliation with God through his shed blood. Jesus' blood is the means by which humanity is redeemed from the power of sin and death, leading to eternal life.

The Power in his blood of Jesus:

For whatever is born of God overcomes the world. And this is the victory that has overcome the world—our faith. (1 John5:4)

The Blood of Jesus has the power to speak.

It has power to Redeemed from the hands of Satan.(Ephesians 1:7)

The blood of Jesus is also seen as a powerful weapon in spiritual warfare, used to overcome the forces of evil. the blood establishes a new covenant (1cor 11:23-25) and Personal

Transformation Believers are called to live in accordance with the power and grace of Jesus' blood, seeking to reflect his love and character in their lives. "But with the precious blood of Christ, as of a lamb without blemish and without spot:" (1 Peter 1:19).

What did blood of Jesus did for you?

My debt is paid, once and for all. (Hebrews 9:28)

I am justified. (Romans 5:9)

I am forgiven. (Ephesians 1:7)

I am spared from God’s wrath.(Romans 5:9)

Jesus testifies on my behalf that I am clean. (Revelation 1:5)

I have been declared righteous. (2 Corinthians 5:21)

( Revelation 12:11) And they overcame him by the blood of the Lamb, and by the word of their testimony; and they loved not their lives unto the death.





















Course 4: Salvation

This is based on the faithful testimony of the holy Spirit in the spirit of believers in Christ, by producing spiritual consciousness that you are saved. (Rom.5.10) " For if, when we were enemies, we were reconciled to God by the death of his Son, much more, being reconciled, we shall be saved by his life".

Salvation is a central theme in Christianity, representing God's plan to rescue humanity from sin and its consequences.

Understanding Salvation

1. God's love: Salvation is rooted in God's love for humanity, demonstrated through Jesus' sacrifice (John 3:16).

2. Sin and separation: Sin separates us from God, but salvation bridges this gap (Romans 3:23, Isaiah 59:2).

3. Jesus' sacrifice: Jesus' death and resurrection provide salvation, reconciling us with God (1 Corinthians 15:34).

The Aspects of Salvation:

1. Forgiveness: Salvation brings forgiveness of sins, freeing us from guilt and shame (Ephesians 1:7).

2. Reconciliation: We are reconciled with God, restored to a right relationship (2 Corinthians 5:18-19).

3. New life: Salvation brings new life in Christ, empowering us to live for God (2 Corinthians 5:17).



Salvation is Received by:

1. Faith: Salvation is received through faith in Jesus Christ (Ephesians2:8-9).

2. Repentance: Repentance is a crucial aspect of salvation, turning from sin to God (Luke 13:3).

3. Assurance: Believers can have assurance of salvation, knowing they are saved through faith in Jesus (1 John 5:13).

How to Live in Salvation

1. Obedience: Salvation leads to obedience to God's Word, demonstrating our love for Him (John 14:15).

2. Service: Believers are called to serve others, reflecting God's love and compassion (Galatians 5:13).

3. Hope: Salvation brings hope for eternal life, giving us confidence in God's promises (Titus 1:2).

4. Witness: Believers are empowered to share the Gospel, witnessing to God's love and salvation (Acts 1:8).



The Process of Salvation

1. Conviction of sin: Recognizing our sinful state and need for salvation (Romans 3:23).

2. Repentance: Turning away from sin and toward God (Luke 13:3).

3. Faith: Placing trust in Jesus Christ as Savior and Lord (Ephesians 2:9).

The Benefits of Salvation

1. Forgiveness: Salvation brings forgiveness of sins, freeing us from guilt and shame (Ephesians 1:7).

2. Reconciliation: We are reconciled with God, restored to a right relationship (2 Corinthians 5:1819).

3. Eternal life: Salvation brings eternal life, giving us hope and confidence in God's promises (John 3:16).



The Impact of Salvation

1. New identity: Believers have a new identity in Christ, becoming children of God (Romans 8:14-17).

2. Transformed life: Salvation leads to a transformed life, characterized by love, joy, and obedience to God (2 Corinthians 5:17).

3. Hope and assurance: Believers have hope and assurance of eternal life, knowing they are saved through faith in Jesus (1 John 5:13).

Summation: Salvation is a powerful and life changing gift from God. May we continually reflect on its significance and live lives that honor Him.







Course 5: New Creature

"Therefore, if anyone is in Christ, he is a new creation; old things have passed away; behold, all things have become new.” (2 Corinthians 5:17)

The new creation does not have two natures – the sinful and holy nature in his heart. No one can have both! The New Creation has only God’s kind of nature in his heart. Therefore, the new creation is no longer a slave of sin, but a slave of righteousness." But God be thanked that though you were slaves of sin, yet you obeyed from the heart that form of doctrine to which you were delivered. And having been set free from sin, you became slaves of righteousness. (Romans 6:17-18)

There is no part of the believer's life from which the newness should be absent. A decided change takes place in the best as well as in the worst. . All men may become new creatures in Christ. The vilest can be recreated equally with the most moral. This newness is not to be waited for till we enter another world. It belongs to this sphere in which we now are. Unless we are new creatures in this world we shall not be new creatures in another. It is on earth that "new creatures" are specially needed.

Characteristics of the New Creation

1. Love: The new creation is characterized by love, reflecting God's nature (1 John 4:7-8).

2. Holiness: Believers are called to live a life of holiness, separated from sin (1 Peter 1:15-16).

3. Obedience: The new creation demonstrates their faith through obedience to God's Word (John 14:15).



Living as a New Creation

1. Walking in the Spirit: Believers are empowered to walk in the Spirit, living a life pleasing to God (Galatians 5:16-18).

2. Fruit of the Spirit: The new creation bears fruit, demonstrating the transformative power of the Gospel (Galatians 5:22-23).

3. Witness and service: Believers are called to serve others, sharing the Gospel and reflecting God's love (Matthew 5:16).

4. Walking in faith: Believers walk by faith, trusting God's promises and guidance (2 Corinthians 5:7).

5. Obedience: The new creation demonstrates obedience to God's Word, living a life that honors Him (John 14:15).

6. Fruitfulness: Believers bear fruit, reflecting the transformative power of the Gospel (John 15:18).



The Transformation Process

1. Regeneration: Believers are born again, receiving new life in Christ (John 3:36).

2. Renewal: The mind is renewed, and the believer is transformed (Romans 12:2).

3. Sanctification: Believers are set apart, growing in holiness and obedience (1 Thessalonians 4:3).

A New Creation is Empowered by the Holy Spirit

1. Empowerment: Believers are empowered by the Holy Spirit, enabling them to live for God (Acts 1:8).

2. Guidance: The Holy Spirit guides believers, teaching them and reminding them of God's truth (John 14:26).

3. Fruit of the Spirit: The new creation demonstrates the fruit of the Spirit, including love, joy, and peace (Galatians 5:22-23).

Summation: The new creation is the transformation that takes place in a person through Christ. It is not merely becoming a better person; it involves receiving new life in Christ and living according to God’s nature and purpose.







Course 6: Born of Water and Spirit (The Baptism)

Born of Water and Spirit: The Baptism Jesus said," Very truly I tell you, no one can enter the kingdom of God unless they are born of water and the Spirit." (John 3:5)



Understanding Baptism

Baptism is a significant aspect of Christian faith, symbolizing spiritual rebirth and identification with Jesus Christ.

THERE ARE TWO TYPES OF BAPTISM

Water Baptism

1. Symbolism: Water represents cleansing, purification, and death to sin (Ephesians 5:26, Romans 6:34).

2. Command: Jesus commanded baptism (Matthew 28:19).

3. Identification: Baptism identifies us with Jesus' death, burial, and resurrection (Romans 6:35).



Spirit Baptism

1. Regeneration: The Holy Spirit regenerates, giving new life (Titus 3:5).

2. Indwelling: The Spirit dwells within believers, empowering them (1 Corinthians 3:16).

3. Empowerment: The Spirit empowers believers for service and witness (Acts 1:8).

The Connection Water baptism and Spirit baptism are interconnected:

1. Spiritual rebirth: Water baptism symbolizes the spiritual rebirth that occurs through the Holy Spirit.

2. Faith expression: Baptism is an outward expression of faith, while the Spirit's work is inward.

scripture references : Matthew 3:13-17 (Jesus' baptism), Acts 2:38-39 (Peter's sermon on baptism), Romans 6:1-11 (baptism and identification with Christ)

Galatians 3:27 (baptism and putting on Christ)

In John 3:1-21, Jesus converses with Nicodemus, a Pharisee and member of the Jewish ruling council. Jesus tells Nicodemus that to enter the kingdom of God, one must be born again (John 3:3). Nicodemus is puzzled, asking how someone can be born again (John 3:4). Jesus responds by explaining the necessity of being born of water and the Spirit (John 3:5).

Born of Water

The phrase "born of water" can be understood in a few ways:

1. Physical birth: Water may symbolize the waters of physical birth, emphasizing the need for spiritual birth as well.

2. Cleansing: Water represents cleansing and purification, highlighting the need for spiritual cleansing through the Holy Spirit.

3. Baptism: Some interpret "born of water" as a reference to baptism, which symbolizes spiritual rebirth and identification with Jesus Christ.



Born of the Spirit

Being "born of the Spirit" refers to the spiritual rebirth that occurs when one puts their faith in Jesus Christ. This spiritual birth is a work of the Holy Spirit, who regenerates and transforms the individual (Titus 3:5).

The Significance of Spiritual Rebirth

Spiritual rebirth is essential for entering the kingdom of God (John 3:3, 5). It involves:

1. New life: Spiritual rebirth brings new life, characterized by a changed heart and a desire to follow God (2 Corinthians 5:17).

2. Faith: Spiritual rebirth is a result of faith in Jesus Christ, who is the source of eternal life (John 3:16).

3. Transformation: Spiritual rebirth leads to transformation, as the Holy Spirit works to conform believers to the image of Jesus Christ (Romans 8:29).

The Role of Baptism

Baptism is an important aspect of the Christian faith, symbolizing spiritual rebirth and identification with Jesus Christ. Through baptism, believers:

1. Identify with Jesus: Baptism symbolizes identification with Jesus' death, burial, and resurrection (Romans 6:35).

2. Public declaration: Baptism is a public declaration of faith, demonstrating a believer's commitment to follow Jesus (Matthew 28:19).

Summation: Being "born of water and Spirit" signifies the spiritual rebirth that occurs through faith in Jesus Christ. This spiritual birth is a work of the Holy Spirit, who regenerates and transforms believers. Baptism symbolizes this spiritual rebirth and identification with Jesus Christ.

Course 7: Temptation

Temptation is a universal human experience that can lead to sin or growth, depending on how we respond.

Understanding Temptation

1. Definition: Temptation is an enticement to do something wrong or unwise (Matthew 4:1-11).

2. Sources: Temptations can come from within (our own desires), the world (external influences), or Satan (spiritual attacks) (James 1:13-15, 1 Peter 5:8).

3. Purpose: Temptations can test our faith, reveal areas for growth, or lead to sin (1 Corinthians 10:13).

Responding to Temptation

1. Resist: Believers are called to resist temptation, using God's Word and the power of the Holy Spirit (James 4:7).

2. Flee: Sometimes, it's wise to flee from tempting situations or environments (1 Corinthians 6:18).

3. Seek accountability: Surrounding ourselves with supportive believers can help us navigate temptations (Proverbs 27:9).

The Nature of Temptation

1. Universal experience: Temptation is a universal human experience, affecting everyone (1 Corinthians 10:13).

2. Variety of forms: Temptations can take many forms, including emotional, physical, or spiritual (James 1:1415).

3. Deception: Temptations often involve deception, making sin appear attractive or harmless (Genesis 3:16).

The Enemy's Tactics

1. Satan's role: Satan is a tempter, seeking to lead believers astray (Matthew 4:1-11).

2. Worldly influences: The world system can also tempt believers, promoting values contrary to God's Word (1 John 2:15-17).

3. Fleshly desires: Our own fleshly desires can tempt us, leading to sinful behavior (Romans 7:14-25).

Most importantly in Overcoming Temptation we need:

1. God's Word: Scripture provides guidance, wisdom, and strength to overcome temptation (Psalm 119:11).

2. Prayer: Prayer empowers believers to resist temptation and seek God's help (Matthew 26:41).

3. Accountability: Surrounding ourselves with supportive believers can help us navigate temptations (Proverbs 27:9).

Overcoming Temptation

1. God's Word: Scripture provides guidance, wisdom, and strength to overcome temptation (Psalm 119:11).

2. Prayer: Prayer empowers believers to resist temptation and seek God's help (Matthew 26:41).

3. Self-control: Developing self-control and discipline helps believers make wise choices (2 Peter 1:5-7).



Growth through Temptation

1. Testing faith: Temptations can test our faith, revealing areas for growth (1 Peter 1:6-7).

2. Developing self-control: Overcoming temptations helps develop self-control and discipline (2 Peter 1:5-7).

3. Dependence on God: Temptations can drive us to dependence on God, deepening our relationship with Him.



Summation: Temptation is a part of the human experience, but believers are not helpless. Through God's Word, prayer, and self-control, we can overcome temptation and grow in our faith.











Course 8: Prayer and Separation

The Pathway to God's Promises and the Gateway to His Move

Prayer as a Promise and the Move of God

(Jeremiah 33:3), (Matthew 6:6), (Luke 5:16), (Acts 4:31), (Hebrews 10:36).

Introduction

Prayer is not merely a spiritual activity; it is a divine system established by God for fellowship, transformation, and the manifestation of His promises. Throughout Scripture, every move of God was preceded by men and women who separated themselves unto God in prayer.

Separation is the secret place where destinies are formed, promises are received, and God's power is released upon the earth. No man walks deeply with God without first learning to separate himself from distractions and seek God's face.

Prayer is where God reveals His promises, and prayer is also the channel through which those promises become reality.



1. Understanding Separation in Prayer

Separation is the deliberate withdrawal from worldly distractions to seek God wholeheartedly.

Why Separation is Necessary

Separation Creates Spiritual Sensitivity When a believer separates himself unto God, his spiritual senses become sharpened.

(Luke 5:16) Jesus continually withdrew Himself into solitary places and prayed.

Separation Creates Intimacy God reveals His secrets to those who spend time with Him. (Psalm 25:14)

Many believers desire God's power, but few desires God's presence. Power is the product of intimacy.

Separation Produces Transformation No one encounters God consistently and remains the same. (Romans 12:2) The prayer closet is God's transformation room.



2. Prayer as a Promise

Prayer exists because God made a promise, God would never command men to pray if He had no intention of answering.

A. Prayer is an Invitation from God. (Jeremiah 33:3)

"Call unto me, and I will answer thee, and show thee great and mighty things which thou knowest not." Prayer begins with God's invitation; Every prayer meeting is heaven inviting earth into fellowship.

B. Prayer Gives Access to Divine Promises

The promises of God are often activated through prayer; Many promises remain dormant until believers engage God through prayer. (Ezekiel 36:37) God promised Israel restoration, yet He required them to seek Him for it.

C. Prayer Positions Us to Receive

Prayer does not change God's faithfulness; it positions us to receive what He has already promised. (Matthew 7:7-8), (1 John 5:14-15) Prayer is the bridge between God's promise and its manifestation.

Why We Pray to Receive the Promise

A. Prayer Aligns Us with God's Will

Many promises require spiritual alignment. (Matthew 6:10) Prayer brings our desires into agreement with God's purpose.



B. Prayer Builds Capacity

Before God releases a promise, He often develops the vessel.

Abraham received the promise after years of walking with God.

Joseph received the dream but needed preparation before entering the palace.

C. Prayer Sustains Faith

Waiting seasons can weaken faith. Prayer strengthens the believer while awaiting fulfillment. (Hebrews 10:36) Prayer is where faith survives delay.



3. Prayer as the Move of God

Every genuine move of God is born in prayer; Revival does not begin on a platform.

Revival begins in a prayer room.

A. Prayer Invites God's Presence (Acts 4:31)

After they prayed, the place was shaken. The presence of God follows the atmosphere of prayer.



B. Prayer Births Revival (2 Chronicles 7:14)

Revival is God's response to a praying people; When prayer decreases, spiritual fire decreases.

When prayer increases, revival begins.



C. Prayer Releases Divine Power

Prayer is not only communication; it is spiritual legislation. (James 5:16-18)

Elijah prayed and shut the heavens, He prayed again and the heavens opened.

Prayer moves what human strength cannot move.

D. Prayer Brings Divine Intervention (Acts 12:5-11)

Peter was imprisoned, but the church prayed.

While men saw chains, God saw an opportunity for intervention.

Prayer invites heaven into impossible situations.



The Relationship Between Separation and God's Move, Every move of God begins with separated people.

Moses: Separated on Mount Sinai and returned carrying God's glory.

Elijah: Separated himself before confronting the prophets of Baal.

Daniel: Separated himself in prayer and received prophetic revelations.

JESUS: Separated Himself in prayer before beginning His public ministry.

Public impact is always preceded by private encounters.



The Power of Persistent Prayer Produces Results (Luke 18:1)

Men ought always to pray and not faint. Persistence demonstrates faith.

Prayer Engages Spiritual Warfare (Ephesians 6:18)

Prayer enforces Christ's victory against spiritual opposition.

Prayer Releases Breakthrough, Every major breakthrough in Scripture was connected to prayer.

Prayer opens doors that education cannot open. Prayer breaks barriers that human effort cannot break.

Prayer is the meeting place between God's promises and man's faith. Through separation, believers cultivate intimacy with God, receive divine promises, and become carriers of His power.

The move of God does not begin in crowds; it begins in closets. It begins when men and women separate themselves unto God, seek His face, and refuse to let go until heaven responds.

Summation: When prayer becomes a lifestyle, promises become manifestations, intimacy becomes power, and ordinary believers become instruments through whom God moves mightily upon the earth. "Every promise of God has a prayer pathway, and every move of God has a praying people behind it."







Course 9: The Holy Spirit (Life in the Spirit)

Who is the Holy Spirit?

1. Third Person of the Trinity: The Holy Spirit is the third Person of the Godhead, coequal with God the Father and God the Son (Matthew 28:19).

2. Giver of Life: The Holy Spirit gives life, empowering believers to live for God (John 6:63, Romans 8:2).

3. Helper and Comforter: The Holy Spirit is our Helper and Comforter, providing guidance, wisdom, and strength (John 14:16-17).

The Role of the Holy Spirit

1. Conviction of Sin: The Holy Spirit convicts us of sin, leading us to repentance (John 16:8-11).

2. Regeneration: The Holy Spirit regenerates us, giving us new life in Christ (Titus 3:5).

3. Indwelling: The Holy Spirit indwells believers, empowering us to live for God (Romans 8:9).

4. Guidance: The Holy Spirit guides us, teaching us and reminding us of God's truth (John 14:26).

Life in the Spirit

1. Walking in the Spirit: Believers are called to walk in the Spirit, living a life that honors God (Galatians 5:1618).

2. Fruit of the Spirit: The Holy Spirit produces fruit in our lives, including love, joy, peace, and self-control (Galatians 5:22-23).

3. Gifts of the Spirit: The Holy Spirit gives gifts to believers, empowering us to serve others (1 Corinthians 12:4-11).

Empowered by the Holy Spirit

1. Witnessing: The Holy Spirit empowers us to witness for Christ, sharing the Gospel with others (Acts 1:8).

2. Ministry: The Holy Spirit enables us to minister to others, demonstrating God's love and compassion (Galatians 6:2).

3. Prayer: The Holy Spirit helps us pray, interceding for us and guiding us (Romans 8:26-27).

The Ministry of The Holy Spirit

1. Conviction: The Holy Spirit convicts us of sin, righteousness, and judgment (John 16:8-11).

2. Regeneration: The Holy Spirit regenerates us, giving us new life in Christ (Titus 3:5).

3. Indwelling: The Holy Spirit indwells believers, empowering us to live for God (Romans 8:9).

The Fruit of the Spirit

1. Love: The Holy Spirit produces love in our lives, enabling us to love God and others (Galatians 5:22).

2. Joy: The Holy Spirit gives us joy, providing us with a deep sense of satisfaction and contentment (Galatians 5:22).

3. Peace: The Holy Spirit produces peace in our lives, calming our fears and anxieties (Galatians 5:22).

The Gifts of the Spirit

1. Diversity: The Holy Spirit gives diverse gifts to believers, empowering us to serve others (1 Corinthians 12:4-11).

2. Purpose: The gifts of the Spirit are given for a purpose, building up the body of Christ (1 Corinthians 12:7).

3. Operation: The gifts of the Spirit operate through faith, demonstrating God's power (1 Corinthians 12:9-10).



Walking in the Spirit

1. Dependence: Walking in the Spirit requires dependence on the Holy Spirit, surrendering to His guidance (Galatians 5:16-18).

2. Obedience: Walking in the Spirit involves obedience to God's Word, living a life that honors Him (John 14:15).

3. Empowerment: Walking in the Spirit empowers us to live a life that pleases God, producing fruit and demonstrating God's love (Galatians 5:22-23).

Reasons why the Holy Spirit is essential for our spiritual lives:

1. Empowerment: The Holy Spirit empowers us to live for God, overcoming sin and living a life that honors Him (Romans 8:13, Galatians 5:16-18).

2. Guidance: The Holy Spirit guides us, teaching us and reminding us of God's truth (John 14:26, 16:13).

3. Comfort: The Holy Spirit comforts us, providing peace and reassurance in times of difficulty (John 14:16-17, Romans 5:5).

4. Fruitfulness: The Holy Spirit produces fruit in our lives, including love, joy, peace, and self-control (Galatians 5:22-23).

5. Witnessing: The Holy Spirit empowers us to witness for Christ, sharing the Gospel with others (Acts 1:8).

Life without the Holy Spirit:

1. Spiritual weakness: Without the Holy Spirit, we are spiritually weak, unable to overcome sin and live for God (Romans 8:7-8).

2. Lack of guidance: Without the Holy Spirit, we lack guidance, struggling to understand God's truth (John 16:13).

3. No comfort: Without the Holy Spirit, we have no comfort, facing difficulties without peace or reassurance (John 14:16-17).

The Holy Spirit is essential for our spiritual lives, empowering us to live for God, guiding us, comforting us, producing fruit in our lives, and empowering us to witness for Christ. By relying on the Holy Spirit, we can experience a deeper relationship with God and live a life that honors Him.

Receiving the Holy Spirit Biblical Examples

1. Believers in Jesus: The Holy Spirit is received when we believe in Jesus Christ (Acts 2:38, Ephesians 1:13).

2. Faith and repentance: Receiving the Holy Spirit involves faith and repentance, turning to God and trusting in Jesus (Acts 2:38).

The Process before receiving

1. Hearing the Gospel: We hear the Gospel, learning about Jesus Christ and His sacrifice for us (Romans 10:17).

2. Believing in Jesus: We believe in Jesus, trusting in His death and resurrection for our salvation (John 3:16).

3. Receiving the Holy Spirit: When we believe, we receive the Holy Spirit, who indwells us and empowers us to live for God (Acts 2:38, Romans 8:9).

The Gift of the Holy Spirit

Promise: The Holy Spirit is a promise from God, given to believers (Acts 2:39).. Gift: The Holy Spirit is a gift, received by faith (Ephesians 1:13).

Summation: Receiving the Holy Spirit involves believing in Jesus Christ, repenting, and trusting in God's promise. When we receive the Holy Spirit, we are empowered to live for God and experience a deeper relationship with Him.





Course 10: The Making of witnesses/Disciples

The process of making witnesses and disciples involves intentional spiritual growth, mentorship, and equipping believers to share the Gospel with others.

1. Spiritual Multiplication: Focus on multiplying disciples, not just adding numbers (2 Timothy 2:2).

2. Intentional Relationships: Build intentional relationships with others, investing in their spiritual growth (Matthew 28:19-20).

3. Equipping Believers: Equip believers with the tools and training needed to share the Gospel effectively (Ephesians 4:11-12).

Steps to Make Disciples or Witnesses

1. Share the Gospel: Share the Gospel with others, leading them to faith in Jesus Christ (1 Corinthians 15:34).

2. Baptize and Teach: Baptize new believers and teach them to obey God's commands (Matthew 28:19-20).

3. Mentor and Disciple: Mentor and disciple new believers, helping them grow in their faith (2 Timothy 2:2).

4. Equip for Ministry: Equip believers for ministry, helping them discover their gifts and talents (Ephesians 4:11-12).

Characteristics of a Disciple Maker

1. Passionate about Jesus: A disciple maker is passionate about Jesus and His mission (Matthew 28:18-20).

2. Intentional about Relationships: A disciple maker is intentional about building relationships with others (Matthew 28:19-20).

3. Equips Others: A disciple maker equips others with the tools and training needed to share the Gospel effectively (Ephesians 4:11-12).

Benefits of Disciples or Witnesses Making

1. Spiritual Growth: Disciple making promotes spiritual growth, both for the disciple maker and the disciple (2 Peter 3:18).

2. Multiplication: Disciple making leads to multiplication, as new believers are equipped to make disciples themselves (2 Timothy 2:2).

3. Fulfillment of the Great Commission: Disciple making helps fulfill the Great Commission, spreading the Gospel to all nations (Matthew 28:18-20).



What Destroys the Witness or Disciples

Several factors can destroy the witness or disciples, including:

1. Sin and Compromise: Living in sin or compromising one's faith can damage a witness's credibility and effectiveness (1 John 3:9-10, (2 Corinthians 6:14-17).

2. Lack of Spiritual Nourishment: Failing to prioritize spiritual nourishment, such as Bible study and prayer, can lead to spiritual weakness and ineffective witness (Matthew 4:4, Psalm 119:105).

3. Fear and Intimidation: Allowing fear or intimidation to dictate one's actions can hinder a witness's ability to share the Gospel effectively (2 Timothy 1:7, Acts 4:29-31).

4. Worldly Influences: Allowing worldly influences to shape one's values and priorities can compromise a witness's effectiveness (1 John 2:15-17, Romans 12:2).

5. Divisions and Conflicts: Unresolved conflicts and divisions within the church or among believers can damage a witness's credibility and effectiveness (1 Corinthians 3:37, Matthew 12:25).

6. Lack of Accountability: Failing to hold oneself and others accountable for spiritual growth and obedience can lead to spiritual stagnation and ineffective witness (Matthew 18:15-17, Galatians 6:12).

7. Unbelief and Doubt: Allowing unbelief and doubt to take root can undermine a witness's faith and effectiveness (Mark 9:23-24, Hebrews 11:6).



Consequences of Destroying the Witness or Disciples

1. Loss of Credibility: Destroying the witness or disciples can lead to a loss of credibility and effectiveness in sharing the Gospel (Matthew 5:13-16).

2. Spiritual Stagnation: Failing to prioritize spiritual growth and nourishment can lead to spiritual stagnation and ineffective witness (2 Peter 1:58).

3. Damage to Relationships: Unresolved conflicts and divisions can damage relationships within the church and among believers (Matthew 18:15-17).

Restoration and Renewal

1. Repentance and Forgiveness: Repentance and forgiveness are essential for restoration and renewal (1 John 1:9, Matthew 6:14-15).

2. Renewal of Spiritual Practices: Renewing spiritual practices, such as Bible study and prayer, can help restore and revitalize one's witness (Psalm 119:105, Matthew 4:4).

3. Accountability and Support: Surrounding oneself with accountability and support can help maintain spiritual growth and effectiveness (Galatians 6:12, Hebrews 10:24-25).



Summation: several factors can destroy the witness or disciples, including sin, lack of spiritual nourishment, fear, worldly influences, divisions, lack of accountability, and unbelief. However, through repentance, forgiveness, renewal of spiritual practices, and accountability, restoration and renewal are possible.







Course 11: The message & proof of witnesses/Disciples

The message of witnesses/disciples is centered on the Gospel of Jesus Christ. Key aspects include:

1. The Life, Death, and Resurrection of Jesus: The message focuses on Jesus' life, death, and resurrection, highlighting His sacrifice for humanity's sins (1 Corinthians 15:34).

2. Salvation through Faith: The message emphasizes salvation through faith in Jesus Christ, offering forgiveness and eternal life (John 3:16, Ephesians 2:89).

3. Repentance and Transformation: The message calls for repentance and transformation, encouraging people to turn from sin and live a life that honors God (Acts 3:19, 2 Corinthians 5:17).



The proof of witnesses/disciples is demonstrated through their lives and actions. Key aspects include:

1. Transformed Lives: Witnesses/disciples demonstrate transformed lives, showcasing the impact of their faith (2 Corinthians 5:17, Galatians 2:20).

2. Love and Compassion: Witnesses/disciples show love and compassion, reflecting Jesus' teachings (John 13:34-35, 1 John 3:16-18).

3. Integrity and Authenticity: Witnesses/disciples live with integrity and authenticity, demonstrating their commitment to their faith (Matthew 5:37, 2 Corinthians 1:12).

4. Boldness and Courage: Witnesses/disciples exhibit boldness and courage, sharing their faith with others despite challenges (Acts 4:29-31, Ephesians 6:19-20).



Powerful witnessing/discipline involves:

1. Relational Evangelism: Building relationships and sharing the Gospel in a natural, relational way (Acts 17:26-27, John 4:7-26).

2. Personal Testimony: Sharing personal testimonies, highlighting the impact of faith on one's life (Acts 26:1-23, 2 Corinthians 12:1-10).

3. Demonstrating God's Love: Demonstrating God's love through acts of service, kindness, and compassion (Matthew 25:31-46, Luke 10:25-37).

4. The Demonstration of Power: The Proof of a Witness and Disciple

God never intended Christianity to be mere words without power. The true witness of Christ is not only known by what he says but by the evidence of God's life working through him.



1. Power is a Proof of Witnessing

Jesus declared that His disciples would receive power to be effective witnesses. (Acts 1:8)

The power of God confirms the message of God. When the Gospel is preached, God often confirms His word through signs, wonders, healing, deliverance, and transformed lives.

2. Miracles Follow True Disciples

A disciple is one who follows Christ, carries His nature, and manifests His works. (Mark 16:17-18)

(John 14:12) Jesus taught that those who believe in Him would continue His works upon the earth.

3. Healing is Evidence of God's Kingdom

Healing demonstrates God's compassion and reveals His kingdom among men. (Matthew 10:7-8)

The ministry of healing is not to glorify men but to reveal Christ and draw people to salvation.

4. Power Flows From Intimacy

The greatest demonstrations of power come from a life of prayer, separation, and fellowship with God. (Luke 9:29),(Acts 4:13)

The apostles carried power publicly because they had first met with God privately.

5. The Greatest Proof is a Transformed Life

While miracles are important, the greatest evidence of discipleship is a life transformed into the image of Christ.

(Galatians 5:22-23), (Matthew 5:16)

Signs and wonders may attract people, but godly character and Christ like living prove genuine discipleship.

A witness of Christ is not known merely by speech but by evidence. The proof of a disciple is seen through a life of prayer, holiness, love, transformed character, and the demonstration of God's power. When a believer abides in Christ, God's presence, power, and fruit become visible through his life.

A disciple is not only one who speaks about Jesus; a disciple is one through whom Jesus can be seen, heard, and demonstrated."

Challenges and Opportunities Witnesses/disciples face such as:

1. Persecution and Opposition: Persecution and opposition can arise when sharing the Gospel or living out one's faith (Matthew 5:10-12, Acts 14:19-20).

2. Cultural and Social Barriers: Cultural and social barriers can hinder effective witnessing/discipline (Acts 15:1-21, Galatians 2:11-14).



The Message of Witnesses/Disciples

The message of witnesses/disciples is rooted in the Gospel of Jesus Christ, which includes:

1. The Love of God: God's love for humanity, demonstrated through the sacrifice of Jesus Christ (John 3:16).

2. The Sinfulness of Humanity: The message acknowledges humanity's sinfulness and need for redemption (Romans 3:23).

3. The Redemption through Jesus Christ: The message emphasizes redemption through faith in Jesus Christ, who died for humanity's sins and rose from the dead (1 Corinthians 15:34).

4. The Call to Repentance: The message calls people to repentance, turning away from sin and towards God (Acts 3:19).



The Importance of Witnesses/Disciples play a crucial role in:

1. Spreading the Gospel: Witnesses/disciples spread the Gospel, sharing the message of Jesus Christ with others (Matthew 28:18-20).

2. Making Disciples: Witnesses/disciples make disciples, helping others to grow in their faith and become followers of Jesus Christ (Matthew 28:18-20).

3. Demonstrating God's Love: Witnesses/disciples demonstrate God's love, showing compassion and kindness to others (Matthew 25:31-46).

However, these challenges also present opportunities for:

1. Growth and Maturity: Overcoming challenges can lead to growth and maturity in one's faith (James 1:24).

2. Effective Witnessing: Effective witnessing can lead to positive outcomes, such as people coming to faith or growing in their relationship with God (Acts 2:41-47).

Summation: the message and proof of witnesses/disciples are centered on the Gospel of Jesus Christ and demonstrated through transformed lives, love, integrity, and boldness. By spreading the Gospel, making disciples, and demonstrating God's love, witnesses/disciples can fulfill their role and advance God's kingdom.



THE KINGDOM — THE PURPOSE OF THE JOURNEY

The Kingdom of God begins with the King. God is the sovereign King, and His Kingdom speaks of His rule, authority, will, and purpose. The Gospel reveals Jesus Christ as the One through whom God's saving purpose and Kingdom are made known. When Jesus began His earthly ministry, He proclaimed the gospel of the Kingdom of God, calling people to repentance and faith: “The kingdom of God is at hand: repent ye, and believe the gospel” (Mark 1:14–15).

To know the King is therefore more than knowing about Him. It is to come under His rule, receive His life, and learn to live according to His will. Jesus taught His followers, “Seek ye first the kingdom of God, and his righteousness” (Matthew 6:33). The Kingdom is not something added to our purpose; it gives purpose its proper direction.

We were not created merely to pursue our own plans, build earthly names, or live for temporary achievements. We were created by God and for His purpose. Our calling, gifts, work, ministry, influence, and ambitions find their true meaning when they are surrendered to the will of God. Jesus said, “Not every one that saith unto me, Lord, Lord, shall enter into the kingdom of heaven; but he that doeth the will of my Father” (Matthew 7:21).

This is why the journey of salvation must lead to a life of obedience, discipleship, and witness. Christ does not save us merely to become spectators; He makes us His witnesses. He said, “Ye shall receive power, after that the Holy Ghost is come upon you: and ye shall be witnesses unto me” (Acts 1:8). We are therefore called to carry the message of Christ, make disciples, and allow the reality of His Kingdom to be seen through our lives (Matthew 28:18–20).

The Kingdom must not remain only a message we proclaim; it must become a life we demonstrate. When truth is lived, righteousness is pursued, love is expressed, holiness is maintained, and Christ is faithfully represented, the character of the King becomes visible through His people. We are called to be “ambassadors for Christ” (2 Corinthians 5:20), representing Him faithfully in the world.

This is where our purpose becomes greater than ourselves. We are not here merely to discover what we can accomplish; we are here to fulfill what God has entrusted to us. We are stewards, witnesses, servants, and representatives of the King. The world and its desires are passing away, but the one who does the will of God abides forever (1 John 2:17).

The Kingdom also gives us an eternal perspective. We are not here forever; our citizenship is in heaven (Philippians 3:20). Christ is coming again, and Scripture points toward the day when “the kingdoms of this world are become the kingdoms of our Lord, and of his Christ” (Revelation 11:15). What begins in us as surrender to the King will ultimately find its fullness in the eternal reign and purpose of God.

Therefore, the question is not only, “What is my purpose?”

The deeper question is:

“What has God written concerning me, and how will I fulfill His will as a servant of His Kingdom?”

This is the path of life: to know the King, to live under His will, to carry His message, to become His witness, and to remain faithful to the end.

The calling is not greater than the King.

The ministry is not greater than the Kingdom.

Our purpose finds its meaning in the will of God.







Course 12: Heaven & Paradise

Heaven and Paradise are concepts deeply rooted in Christian theology, representing eternal life with God.

Heaven is described in the Bible as:

1. God's Dwelling Place: Heaven is God's dwelling place, where He resides in glory and majesty (Psalm 103:19, Isaiah 66:1).

2. Eternal Life: Heaven represents eternal life, where believers will live forever with God, free from suffering, pain, and sin (John 14:23, Revelation 21:4).

3. A Place of Joy and Worship: Heaven is depicted as a place of joy, worship, and fellowship with God and the saints (Revelation 7:9-12, Psalm 100:45).

Paradise

Paradise is often used interchangeably with Heaven, but it can also refer to:

1. The Intermediate State: Some interpretations suggest Paradise refers to the intermediate state between death and resurrection, where believers experience peace and joy in God's presence (Luke 23:43, 2 Corinthians 5:8).

2. Eternal Bliss: Paradise is also described as a state of eternal bliss, where believers will enjoy God's presence and fellowship forever (Revelation 21:3-4).



Key Aspects of Heaven and Paradise

1. Eternal Fellowship: Heaven and Paradise offer eternal fellowship with God and the saints (Revelation 21:34, John 17:3).

2. No Suffering or Pain: Heaven and Paradise are characterized by the absence of suffering, pain, and sin (Revelation 21:4, Isaiah 35:10).

3. Joy and Worship: Heaven and Paradise are places of joy, worship, and adoration of God (Revelation 7:9-12, Psalm 100:45).



Implications for Believers

1. Hope and Encouragement: The promise of Heaven and Paradise offers hope and encouragement for believers, motivating them to live faithfully and share the Gospel with others (1 :13-18, Philippians 3:20-21).

2. Eternal Perspective: The promise of Heaven and Paradise provides an eternal perspective, helping believers prioritize what truly matters in life (Matthew 6:1921, Colossians 3:12).

Descriptions of Heaven The Bible describes Heaven as:

1. A Place of Beauty: Heaven is depicted as a place of unparalleled beauty, with descriptions of gold, jewels, and radiant light (Revelation 21:1821).

2. A Place of Peace: Heaven is characterized as a place of perfect peace, where there is no conflict, suffering, or pain (Revelation 21:4, Isaiah 35:10).

3. A Place of Worship: Heaven is a place of worship, where angels and saints praise and adore God (Revelation 4:811, 5:11-14).



The Nature of Heaven

1. Eternal: Heaven is eternal, with no beginning or end (Psalm 102:27, Revelation 1:8).

2. Spiritual: Heaven is a spiritual realm, where God dwells in His glorified presence (John 4:24, 1 Corinthians 15:44-49).

3. Glory: Heaven is filled with God's glory, radiating His presence and majesty (Isaiah 6:13, Revelation 15:8).

Paradise as a Present Experience

While Paradise is often associated with the afterlife, some interpretations suggest that believers can experience a foretaste of Paradise in their present lives through:

1. Intimacy with God: Believers can experience intimacy with God through prayer, worship, and obedience (John 14:21-23, Psalm 16:11).

2. The Holy Spirit: The Holy Spirit dwells within believers, providing a present experience of God's presence and peace (Romans 8:911, Galatians 5:22-23).

Summation: Heaven and Paradise represent the ultimate hope and destination for believers, offering eternal life, joy, and fellowship with God. May these concepts inspire and motivate you to live a life that honors God!

Questions and Reflections

1. What does the promise of Heaven and Paradise mean to you personally?

2. How does the eternal perspective of Heaven and Paradise influence your daily decisions and priorities?









Course 13: Hell

The Bible describes Hell as:

1. A Place of Punishment: Hell is depicted as a place of punishment for those who reject God and live in sin (Matthew 25:41-46, Revelation 20:15).

2. A Place of Darkness: Hell is described as a place of darkness, where there is no light or hope (Matthew 8:12, 22:13).

3. A Place of Fire: Hell is often associated with fire, symbolizing God's judgment and wrath (Matthew 25:41, Mark 9:43-48).

The Nature of Hell

1. Eternal Separation: Hell is characterized as eternal separation from God, where individuals experience the consequences of their choices (2 Thessalonians 1:9, Revelation 20:10).

2. Conscious Suffering: Many interpretations suggest that Hell involves conscious suffering, where individuals are aware of their punishment and separation from God (Luke 16:19-31).

The Purpose of Hell

1. Judgment: Hell serves as a place of judgment, where God renders justice and punishes sin (Romans 2:5-11, Revelation 20:12-15).

2. Separation from God: Hell represents the ultimate consequence of rejecting God and living in sin, resulting in eternal separation from His presence (Matthew 25:41-46).

Implications for Believers

1. Sharing the Gospel: The reality of Hell motivates believers to share the Gospel with others, offering them the opportunity to escape eternal punishment (Matthew 28:18-20, 2 Corinthians 5:18-21).

2. Living with Purpose: The awareness of Hell encourages believers to live with purpose, prioritizing their relationship with God and living a life that honors Him (Matthew 6:33, Colossians 3:12).

The Reality of Hell

The Bible teaches that Hell is a real place, where individuals who reject God and live in sin will face eternal punishment. This reality should motivate us to:

1. Share the Gospel: Believers should share the Gospel with others, offering them the opportunity to escape eternal punishment.

2. Live with Purpose: The awareness of Hell should encourage us to live with purpose, prioritizing our relationship with God and living a life that honors Him.

The Nature of Hell The e Bible describes Hell as a place of:

1. Darkness: Hell is characterized as a place of darkness, where there is no light or hope.

2. Fire: Hell is often associated with fire, symbolizing God's judgment and wrath.

3. Torment: Hell is described as a place of torment, where individuals experience eternal suffering.

The Duration of Hell

The Bible teaches that Hell is an eternal place, where individuals will face punishment forever. This emphasizes the importance of:

1. Making a Decision: Individuals must make a decision about their relationship with God, choosing to accept or reject Him.

2. Living with Eternity in View: Believers should live with eternity in view, prioritizing their relationship with God and living a life that honors Him.



The reality of Hell has significant implications for believers, including:

1. Evangelism: Believers should prioritize evangelism, sharing the Gospel with others and offering them the opportunity to escape eternal punishment.

2. Discipleship: Believers should prioritize discipleship, helping others to grow in their relationship with God and live a life that honors Him.



Summation: The concept of Hell is a complex and often debated topic. However, the Bible teaches that Hell is a real place, where individuals who reject God and live in sin will face eternal punishment. This reality should motivate us to share the Gospel, live with purpose, and prioritize our relationship with God



Course 14: Discernment of Falsehood

Discernment of falsehood is crucial in today's world, where misinformation and deception can lead people astray.

Understanding Falsehood

Falsehood can manifest in various forms, including:

1. False Teachings: Teachings that contradict biblical truth or distort God's Word.

2. Deception: Misleading information or lies that deceive people.

3. False Prophets: Individuals who claim to speak for God but deliver false messages.

The Bible provides guidance on discernment, including:

1. Testing Everything: Believers are encouraged to test everything against God's Word (1 Thessalonians 5:21-22).

2. Discerning Spirits: Believers are called to discern spirits, recognizing whether they are from God or not (1 John 4:13).

3. Knowing God's Voice: Believers can develop a relationship with God, learning to recognize His voice and distinguish it from false voices (John 10:27).

Practical ways for Discernment

1. Know God's Word: Familiarize yourself with the Bible, understanding its teachings and principles.

2. Seek Guidance: Seek guidance from spiritual leaders, mentors, or the Holy Spirit.

3. Evaluate Sources: Critically evaluate sources of information, considering their credibility and alignment with God's Word.

Consequences of Not Discerning Falsehood

Failing to discern falsehood can lead to:

1. Spiritual Confusion: Believers may become confused about God's truth and teachings.

2. Deception: Believers may be deceived, leading them astray from God's path.

3. Loss of Faith: Repeated exposure to falsehood can erode faith and trust in God.

Empowerment through Discernment Developing discernment empowers believers to:

1. Stand Firm: Stand firm in their faith, resisting false teachings and deception.

2. Make Informed Decisions: Make informed decisions, guided by God's truth and principles.

3. Live with Confidence: Live with confidence, knowing they are grounded in God's truth.

Questions and Reflections

1. How can you develop discernment in your daily life?

2. What are some common false teachings or deceptions you've encountered?



The Importance of Discernment

Discernment is crucial for believers, enabling them to:

1. Distinguish Truth from Error: Discernment helps believers distinguish between truth and error, protecting them from false teachings and deception.

2. Make Wise Decisions: Discernment enables believers to make wise decisions, guided by God's truth and principles.

3. Navigate Complex Situations: Discernment helps believers navigate complex situations, providing clarity and direction.

Developing Discernment

To develop discernment, believers can:

1. Study God's Word: Regularly study the Bible, understanding its teachings and principles.

2. Pray for Wisdom: Pray for wisdom and discernment, seeking God's guidance and direction.

3. Seek Mentorship: Seek guidance from spiritual mentors or leaders, learning from their experiences and insights.



Common obstacles to discernment include:

1. Lack of Knowledge: Limited understanding of God's Word and principles can hinder discernment.

2. Emotional Influences: Emotions can cloud judgment, leading to poor discernment.

3. Cultural Influences: Cultural pressures and norms can influence discernment, leading to compromise.



Cultivating Discernment

To cultivate discernment, believers can:

1. Practice Self-reflection: Regularly reflect on their thoughts, emotions, and actions.

2. Seek Feedback: Seek feedback from trusted friends, mentors, or leaders.

3. Stay Grounded in God's Word: Regularly study and apply God's Word, staying grounded in its truth and principles.









Course 15: The World

In the Bible, "The World" refers to:

1. The fallen world system: A system opposed to God, characterized by sin, rebellion, and darkness (1 John 2:15-17, Romans 1:18-32).

2. The world's values and priorities: Values and priorities that contradict God's values, such as materialism, pride, and self-centeredness (Matthew 6:24, 1 John 2:15-17).

Relationship with the World Believers are called to:

1. Not conform to the world: Avoid adopting the world's values and priorities (Romans 12:2).

2. Be in the world but not of it: Engage with the world while maintaining a distinct identity as followers of Christ (John 17:14 -16).



The World's Influence through:

1. Cultural pressures: Societal norms and expectations that may contradict God's truth.

2. Materialism: Prioritizing material possessions and wealth over spiritual pursuits.

3. Moral relativism: Rejecting absolute moral standards and embracing moral ambiguity.

Overcoming the World's Influence

Believers can overcome the world's influence by:

1. Seeking God's truth: Prioritizing God's Word and principles.

2. Living a life of obedience: Obeying God's commands and living a life that honors Him.

3. Cultivating a heavenly perspective: Focusing on eternal realities and priorities.

Questions and Reflections

1. How do you see the world's influence in your life?

2. What strategies can you use to maintain a heavenly perspective and resist the world's influence?



The World's System vs. God's Kingdom

The world's system and God's Kingdom have distinct values, priorities, and principles. Believers must navigate this tension, recognizing that:

1. The world's system is temporary: The world's values and priorities are fleeting and will pass away (1 John 2:17).

2. God's Kingdom is eternal: God's Kingdom and its values are eternal, and believers are called to prioritize eternal realities (Matthew 6:33).



The Danger of Conformity

Conformity to the world's system can lead to:

1. Loss of identity: Believers may lose their distinct identity as followers of Christ.

2. Compromise: Believers may compromise their values and principles, leading to spiritual stagnation.

Living as a Stranger in the World Believers are called to live as strangers in the world, recognizing that:

1. Our citizenship is in heaven: Believers are citizens of God's Kingdom, and their ultimate allegiance is to God (Philippians 3:20).

2. We are ambassadors for Christ: Believers are ambassadors for Christ, representing Him in the world (2 Corinthians 5:20).



Practical Applications To live out their faith effectively, believers can:

1. Prioritize God's Word: Study and apply God's Word, seeking to understand its teachings and principles.

2. Cultivate community: Surround themselves with a community of believers who can provide support, encouragement, and accountability.

3. Live with intentionality: Live with intentionality, prioritizing eternal realities and making decisions that align with God's will.

Questions and Reflections

1. How can you prioritize God's Kingdom values in your daily life?

2. What are some practical ways to live as a stranger in the world, representing Christ effectively?









Course 16: Godly Ambition

Understanding Godly Ambition :

Matthew 6:33 — “But seek first the kingdom of God and his righteousness, and all these things will be added to you.”

Colossians 3:23–24 teaches believers to work wholeheartedly as unto the Lord, because ultimately our reward comes from Him.

WHAT IS GODLY AMBITION?

Godly ambition is a strong desire to accomplish something significant for God's glory, according to God's purpose, and through God's principles.

Ambition itself is not automatically evil. The question is:

Who is at the center of your ambition—God or yourself?

Paul had tremendous ambition. He said:

Romans 15:20 — “And so I have made it my ambition to preach the gospel…”

Paul was ambitious, but his ambition was not to become famous. His ambition was to fulfill God's assignment.

Therefore:

Worldly ambition says: “I want to become great so people will know me.”

Godly ambition says: “I want to become effective so God can use me.”

That distinction is extremely important.

GODLY AMBITION IS FOCUSED ON GOD'S PURPOSE

A person with godly ambition does not merely ask: “What do I want to achieve?”

They ask: “What does God want to accomplish through my life?”

Ephesians 2:10 says that we are God's workmanship, created in Christ Jesus for good works that God prepared beforehand.

This means your life is not an accident. God has purposes He wants to accomplish through you.

Jesus as our greatest example, Jesus understood His assignment.

John 4:34: “My food is to do the will of him that sent me, and to finish his work.”

His ambition was connected to the Father's will.

Before pursuing a dream, ask: Is this God's purpose or simply my desire?

Will this bring glory to God? Can God use this ambition to bless other people?

Am I willing to surrender it if God redirects me?

GODLY AMBITION IS DRIVEN BY LOVE FOR GOD

The motivation behind your ambition matters.

Two people may pursue exactly the same goal but have completely different motivations.

One may want influence because they want people to worship them.

Another may desire influence because they want to use that influence to point people toward Christ.

(1 Corinthians 10:31) “Whether therefore ye eat, or drink, or whatsoever ye do, do all to the glory of God.”

The question is not simply: “What am I building?” The deeper question is: “Why am I building it?”

Godly ambition flows from love for God.

GODLY AMBITION IS GUIDED BY SCRIPTURE

Not every opportunity is a God opportunity. Not every dream is a divine assignment.

Not everything that increases your popularity increases your usefulness to God.

(Psalm 119:105) God's Word is a lamp to our feet and a light to our path.

Therefore, ambition must be submitted to Scripture.

If your ambition requires dishonesty, manipulation, sexual immorality, hatred, pride, exploitation, or disobedience to God, it cannot be called godly ambition.

Proverbs 3:5–6 teaches us to trust God rather than depending entirely on our own understanding.

CHARACTERISTICS OF GODLY AMBITION

A. HUMILITY

Godly ambition does not mean thinking you are better than everyone else.

It means recognizing that everything you have ultimately comes from God.

James 4:6: “God resist the proud, but give grace unto the humble.”

David had a great desire to build a house for God, but God ultimately chose Solomon to build the temple. David's response demonstrates something powerful: he could support God's purpose even when he would not personally receive the credit.

That is maturity. A test of godly ambition:

Can you celebrate what God is doing through someone else?

If yes, your ambition is becoming healthier.

B. INTEGRITY

Godly ambition refuses to sacrifice character for achievement. You should never become successful at the expense of your soul.

Proverbs 10:9 says: “He that walks uprightly walks surely…”

Luke 16:10 teaches that faithfulness in little things matters.

Your character must grow alongside your platform. Because: A large platform with a small character can become dangerous.

God is interested not only in what you accomplish but also in who you become while accomplishing it.

C. FAITHFULNESS

Godly ambition understands that great things often begin with small acts of obedience.

David did not begin as king. He was first faithful with sheep.

Joseph did not begin in the palace. He passed through difficult seasons before entering his place of influence. Luke 16:10 teaches faithfulness in little things.

Do not despise small beginnings. (Zechariah 4:10) “For who hath despised the day of small things?”

Your current assignment may be preparation for a greater assignment.

GODLY AMBITION AND THE MEDIA SPACE

This is especially important for today's generation.

The media space can become either a platform for self-glorification or a tool for kingdom transformation.

Social media can tempt people to chase: likes, followers, views, recognition, popularity, validation, and personal branding.

None of these things are automatically sinful.

The danger comes when visibility becomes more important than purpose.

The question should not only be:

“How many people watched me?” But “What happened to the people who watched me?”

Did they become encouraged?

Did they learn something?

Did they encounter truth?

Did they become inspired to pursue God?

Did their lives become better?

Did the content produce transformation?

MEDIA SHOULD BECOME A MISSION FIELD

Matthew 28:19–20 gives the Church the Great Commission.

Today, the mission field is not only the physical street, marketplace, school, or community.

The digital space is also where people spend their time, consume ideas, learn values, and form worldviews.

Therefore, Christians should not simply ask: “How can I become famous online?”

We should ask: “How can God use my digital presence to influence people for His purposes?”

Your phone can become a tool, Your camera can become a tool, Your editing skills can become a tool, Your microphone can become a tool, Your social media page can become a tool, Your creativity can become a tool.

The issue is what purpose you are using them for.

TRANSFORMATION OVER ATTENTION

This should become one of the major principles of the course:

Godly ambition seeks transformation, not merely attention. Attention is not necessarily impact.

You can have millions of views and change nobody.

You can also reach a smaller audience and genuinely transform lives.

Matthew 5:16 teaches believers to let their light shine so that people may see their good works and glorify the Father.

Therefore, Christian media should aim for:

Attention → Connection → Truth → Transformation. The goal is not simply to make people watch. The goal is to give people something that can change how they think, live, believe, and act.

THE BENEFITS OF GODLY AMBITION

1. PURPOSE AND DIRECTION: When God's purpose becomes the center of your ambition, you gain direction.

Proverbs 19:21 reminds us that although people make plans, God's purpose ultimately prevails.

2. MOTIVATION: Purpose gives you strength to continue when things become difficult. Paul experienced persecution, rejection, hardship, and opposition, yet continued because he understood his assignment. Acts 20:24

3. FULFILLMENT AND JOY: True fulfillment does not come simply from achieving personal goals. Jesus said: John 15:11 that His joy could be in His followers and their joy could be full.

There is a special joy that comes from knowing: “I am doing what God created me to do.”

GODLY AMBITION VS WORLDLY AMBITION

God's glory

Self-glory

God's purpose

Personal gain

Service

Self-promotion

Character

Image

Faithfulness

Competition

Impact

Recognition

Contentment

Constant comparison

Obedience

Compromise




Transformation Attention

Philippians 2:3–4 warns believers against selfish ambition and calls them to humility and concern for others. This is one of the clearest Scriptures for understanding the difference.





BIBLICAL EXAMPLES OF GODLY AMBITION

David had a desire to build a house for God. (1 Chronicles 282–3) shows David's heart concerning the temple. Although God did not permit D:avid to build it himself, David prepared resources and encouraged Solomon.

Godly ambition is not always about receiving credit for the assignment. Sometimes your role is to prepare the way for someone else.

Paul had extraordinary missionary ambition. (Romans 15:20) shows his desire to preach where Christ had not yet been proclaimed. His ambition was connected to the Great Commission.

His question was not: “How can I become the most famous apostle?”

His focus was: “How can the Gospel reach more people?”

Nehemiah saw the broken walls of Jerusalem and became burdened to rebuild them.

Nehemiah 2:18 shows the people responding to the vision: “Let us rise up and build.”

Nehemiah demonstrates how godly ambition can turn burden into vision and vision into action.



COMMON ENEMIES OF GODLY AMBITION

1. SELFISHNESS: When your ambition becomes entirely about yourself, it can become destructive.

(James 3:16) connects selfish ambition with disorder and harmful practices.

2. FEAR: Fear can prevent someone from pursuing what God has placed before them.

(2 Timothy 1:7) reminds believers that God has not given us the spirit of fear, but of power, love, and a sound mind.

3. COMPARISON: Social media has made comparison easier than ever. You see another person's success and begin questioning your own journey. But (Galatians 6:4) encourages believers to examine their own work rather than measuring themselves against others.

4. PRIDE: Success can become dangerous when the person begins believing they no longer need God. (Deuteronomy 8:18) reminds us that it is God who gives the ability to produce wealth.

HOW TO CULTIVATE GODLY AMBITION

— PRAY: Ask God “Lord, what do You want to accomplish through my life?” James 1:5 teaches us to ask God for wisdom.

— STUDY THE WORD: Your ambition needs biblical boundaries. (2 Timothy 3:16–17)

— DISCOVER YOUR ASSIGNMENT

Ask: What burden has God placed in my heart?, What gifts has He given me?, What problems can I help solve?, Who has God called me to serve?, What kingdom purpose can my skills fulfill?

— DEVELOP YOUR SKILLS: Spirituality does not eliminate excellence. (Proverbs 22:29) speaks about the person who is diligent and skilled in their work.

If God gives you a media assignment, develop your media skills.

If God gives you a teaching assignment, study.

If God gives you leadership, develop leadership.

Anointing and excellence should work together.

— REMAIN ACCOUNTABLE: Surround yourself with mature believers who can correct you.

(Proverbs 11:14) emphasizes the value of wise counsel.

— STAY FAITHFUL: Don't abandon your assignment because the results are slow.

Galatians 6:9 teaches believers not to become weary in doing good.

Summation: Godly ambition is the desire to become all that God has called you to become, accomplish what He has assigned you to accomplish, and use your influence to bring Him glory and transform lives.

And for the media generation: Don't build a platform merely to be seen. Build a platform that gives people something worth seeing, hearing, learning, and becoming. (Matthew 5:16) Let your light shine before people, so that they may see your good works and glorify your Father in heaven.

That should be the heart of the course: not ambition for visibility, but ambition for God's purpose; not influence for ego, but influence for transformation.







Course 17: Divine Guidance

INTRODUCTION

Divine guidance is the supernatural privilege of being led by God in the decisions, direction, relationships, assignments, and purposes of our lives. God does not desire His children to walk blindly. He desires us to know His will, recognize His leading, and follow His direction.

Proverbs 3:5–6 teaches us to trust in the Lord rather than depend completely on our own understanding, promising that He will direct our paths. Divine guidance is therefore more than asking God, “What should I do?” It is developing such a relationship with God that our hearts become sensitive to His voice and our lives become willing to obey His direction.

Divine guidance is not merely knowing where God is taking you; it is knowing God well enough to trust Him while He leads you.

UNDERSTANDING DIVINE GUIDANCE as God's Direction: Divine guidance is God's direction for our lives according to His purpose and wisdom. God sees what we cannot see. He knows the beginning from the end and understands the consequences of decisions we have not yet made. (Isaiah 46:10), (Psalm 32:8) (Proverbs 16:9 A person may plan his way, but the Lord directs his steps. This means that planning is not wrong. However, our plans must remain submitted to God's wisdom.

There is a need for Spiritual Discernment: Spiritual discernment is the ability to distinguish what is from God, what is merely from our own desires, and what does not agree with God's truth. (Hebrews 5:14) teaches that spiritual maturity develops the ability to discern good and evil. (Romans 12:2 teaches that the renewal of our minds helps us discern the will of God.

Divine Guidance Requires Relationship: Guidance is deeply connected to relationship. (John 10:27 — His sheep hear His voice, He knows them, and they follow Him. The goal is therefore not merely to receive instructions from God but to know God.

The closer we walk with God, the more sensitive we become to His direction.

SOURCES OF DIVINE GUIDANCE ARE :

A. THE WORD OF GOD: The Bible is the primary and foundational standard for divine guidance.(Psalm 119:105) (2 Timothy 3:16–17) God will never lead us in a way that contradicts His revealed Word. If someone believes they have received “guidance” that directly contradicts Scripture, that guidance must be rejected.

B. PRAYER: Prayer is a major pathway through which we seek God's direction. (James 1:5 ),(Philippians 4:6–7)

Prayer changes our posture from: “God, bless what I have already decided.” To “Lord, show me what You desire, and give me grace to obey.”

3. THE HOLY SPIRIT AND DIVINE GUIDANCE: The Holy Spirit plays a vital role in guiding believers.

(John 16:13) (Romans 8:14) The Holy Spirit can bring conviction, understanding, wisdom, spiritual sensitivity, and direction.

We see examples of Spirit-led direction in the early church. (Acts 13:2–4) While believers were worshipping and fasting, the Holy Spirit directed them concerning the ministry of Barnabas and Saul. (Acts 16:6–10) Paul and his companions experienced the Spirit preventing them from going into certain regions before receiving direction concerning where they should go.

However, spiritual impressions should always be tested against Scripture and godly wisdom.

4. Godly Wisdom and Counsel : (Proverbs 11:14; Proverbs 15:22) God can use mature believers and wise counsel to help us see what we may not see ourselves.

OBSTACLES TO DIVINE GUIDANCE

A. SIN AND DISOBEDIENCE: Persistent disobedience can damage our fellowship with God and make our spiritual sensitivity weaker. Isaiah 59:1–2 speaks about sin creating separation in the relationship between God and His people. The answer is repentance. 1 John 1:9 teaches that God is faithful to forgive and cleanse those who confess their sins.

B. DISTRACTION AND BUSYNES: A noisy life can produce a distracted heart. We can become so occupied with school, work, social media, entertainment, relationships, and other responsibilities that we neglect time with God. Jesus often withdrew to quiet places to pray. (Luke 5:16)

C. LACK OF TRUST: Sometimes God gives direction, but we hesitate because we do not trust Him. (Proverbs 3:5–6) calls us to trust God rather than lean entirely on our own understanding. So always talk Faith by saying: “I may not understand everything God is doing, but I trust the One who is leading me.”

D. FEAR: Fear can cause us to reject God's direction because obedience may require courage. (2 Timothy 1:7) reminds believers that God has not given us a spirit of fear, but of power, love, and a sound mind.

E. PERSONAL DESIRE: One of the hardest things in divine guidance is distinguishing God's will from our own desires.

Jeremiah 17:9 warns about the deceptive nature of the human heart.Therefore, we must surrender our desires to God rather than asking God to simply approve them.

F. IMPATIENCE : Sometimes we want immediate answers. But God's timing is part of His wisdom.

Psalm 27:14 encourages us to wait on the Lord and remain courageous.

Waiting is not necessarily divine rejection but Sometimes waiting is part of God's guidance.

CULTIVATING A LIFE OF DIVINE GUIDANCE

1. DEVELOP A DEEP RELATIONSHIP WITH GOD: Guidance begins with relationship. Spend consistent time: Reading Scripture,

Praying, Worshipping, Meditating on God's Word, Repenting when necessary, Giving thanks, Fellowshipping with mature believers. ( John 15:4–5) .

2. DEVELOP SPIRITUAL SENSITIVITY: The more we expose ourselves to God's Word and presence, the more our thinking becomes shaped by His truth.(Romans 12:2)Spiritual sensitivity is not merely an emotional experience. It is a life increasingly shaped by God's truth.

3. ASK FOR WISDOM (James 1:5) part of your lifestyle. Do not be ashamed to admit: “Lord, I don't know what to do. Give me wisdom.” God is not intimidated by our questions.

4. WALK IN OBEDIENCE : Obedience strengthens our ability to recognize what God desires.

John 14:15 connects love for Christ with obedience to Him; do not wait for spectacular guidance when God has already given you a clear command in Scripture.

5. TRUST GOD'S SOVEREIGNTY : God is not confused about your future. (Psalm 139:16) speaks of God's knowledge of our days. Romans 8:28 reminds believers that God works in all things for the good of those who love Him and are called according to His purpose. Therefore, we can surrender the future to God.

IMPORTANT PRINCIPLES TO REMEMBER

God's guidance will never contradict God's Word.

God's guidance should draw us closer to Christ, not away from Him.

Not every strong feeling is divine guidance.

Prayer should accompany important decisions.

Wisdom and godly counsel are valuable tools for discernment.

Sometimes God gives direction one step at a time.

Waiting can be part of God's guidance.

Divine guidance requires obedience.

We should seek God's will rather than merely seek God's permission for our own will.

The greatest guidance is not simply knowing God's plan but knowing God Himself.



Summation: Divine Guidance = God's Word + Prayer + Holy Spirit + Discernment + Wisdom + Obedience + Trust. The goal of divine guidance is not merely to know God's direction; it is to walk faithfully with God.





Course 18: His Coming & His Rewards

The Promise of His Coming The Bible promises that Jesus will return:

1. Visibly: Jesus will return visibly, just like He ascended (Acts 1:9-11).

2. Triumphantly: Jesus will return in triumph, with power and great glory (Matthew 24:30).



The rewards of Jesus' coming include:

1. Eternal life: Believers will receive eternal life and live forever with God.

2. Resurrection: Believers who have died will be resurrected, and their bodies will be transformed.

3. Glory and honor: Believers will receive glory and honor in the presence of God.

The Judgment Seat of Christ is a crucial aspect of Jesus' return:

1. Evaluation of works: Believers' works will be evaluated, and they will receive rewards or suffer loss.

2. Rewards for faithful service: Believers who have served faithfully will receive rewards.

Living in Light of His Coming believers should:

1. Be prepared: Be prepared to meet Jesus, living a life that honors Him.

2. Serve faithfully: Serve God and others faithfully, seeking to please Him.

3. Share the Gospel: Share the Gospel with others, pointing them to Jesus.



The significance of Jesus' return and the rewards that come with tithe promise of Jesus' return motivates believers to:

1. Live with purpose: Live a life that honors God and fulfills His purposes.

2. Serve with passion: Serve God and others with passion and dedication.

3. Share the Gospel: Share the Gospel with others, pointing them to Jesus.



The Rewards of Faithfulness include:

1. Crown of life: The crown of life, which is a symbol of eternal life and victory.

2. Crown of glory: The crown of glory, which is a symbol of honor and recognition.

3. Eternal rewards: Eternal rewards that will last forever in God's kingdom.

The Importance of Stewardship is crucial in light of Jesus' return:
