1. Managing resources wisely: Managing resources wisely, including time, talents, and treasures.

2. Investing in God's kingdom: Investing in God's kingdom, seeking to advance His purposes.

3. Living with accountability: Living with accountability, recognizing that we will give an account to God.



Questions and Reflections

1. How can you live a life that honors God and fulfills His purposes?

2. What are some ways you can steward your resources wisely and invest in God's kingdom?









Course 19: Judgment

Understanding Judgment

Judgment refers to God's evaluation of our actions, motives, and hearts. The Bible teaches that judgment is certain and that God will judge all people (Ecclesiastes 12:14, Romans 14:12).

The Judgment Seat of Christ

The Judgment Seat of Christ is a crucial aspect of judgment, where believers' works will be evaluated, and they will receive rewards or suffer loss (2 Corinthians 5:10). This judgment is not about salvation but about accountability for our actions and choices.

Aspects of Judgment involve:

1. Justice: God's justice will be upheld, and wrongdoing will be addressed (Psalm 9:8).

2. Mercy: God's mercy and grace will be applied to believers (Psalm 103:8-10).

3. Accountability: Believers will be held accountable for their actions (Romans 14:12).

The purpose of judgment is:

1. To uphold God's justice: Judgment upholds God's justice and righteousness (Psalm 9:8).

2. To reveal hearts: Judgment reveals the true nature of our hearts and actions (Luke 8:17).

3. To determine rewards: Judgment determines rewards for believers based on their works (1 Corinthians 3:12-15).

The basis of judgment is:

1. God's Word: God's Word is the standard for judgment (John 12:48).

2. Motives and intentions: God's evaluation considers motives and intentions behind actions (Matthew 6:14).

3. Faith and obedience: Faith and obedience to God's commands are crucial (Hebrews 5:9).

Preparing for Judgment, believers should:

1. Live with integrity: Live a life that honors God and reflects His character (Proverbs 10:9).

2. Serve faithfully: Serve God and others faithfully, seeking to please Him (Colossians 3:23-24).

3. Seek forgiveness: Seek forgiveness for sins and shortcomings (1 John 1:9).

Summation: The concept of judgment is a crucial aspect of the Christian faith. Understanding judgment encourages believers to live with integrity, serve faithfully, and seek forgiveness. As we anticipate the Judgment Seat of Christ, let us strive to live lives that honor God and reflect His character.

Scriptural References: (Ecclesiastes 12:14), (Romans 14:12), (2 Corinthians 5:10), (Psalm 9:8), (Psalm 103:8-10), (Romans 14:12).





Course 20: A New Heaven & Earth (The spirit and the bride)

The Spirit and the Bride are key players in God's final invitation to sinners to find salvation in Christ, as seen in Revelation 22:17. Here, the Spirit and the Bride say, "Come!" inviting those who are thirsty to come and drink from the water of life, symbolizing eternal life and salvation through Jesus Christ.



The Role of the Spirit:

The Spirit invites the human race to come to Christ through Scripture,

inspiring the Bible and applying the blood of Christ to sinners' hearts.

The Spirit's role is crucial in salvation, working cooperatively with the Bride (the church) to bring lost sinners to faith in Christ.

The Role of the Bride:

The Bride, representing the church, joins the Spirit in inviting lost sinners to come and drink from Christ, finding life and satisfaction.

The Bride's role is to partner with the Spirit in Gospel outreach, calling thirsty people to faith in Christ.



A New Heaven and Earth:

This concept refers to the ultimate restoration and renewal of all things, where God will dwell with humanity in a new, eternal realm.

In Revelation 21, the Bride is described as the church of Jesus Christ, highlighting the intimate relationship between Christ and His people.

The new heaven and new earth will be characterized by the river of the water of life, flowing from the throne of God and the Lamb, symbolizing eternal life and God's presence.

The Bible teaches about a future time when God will create a new heaven and a new earth, free from sin and suffering (Isaiah 65:17, Revelation 21:1). This new creation will be characterized by:



God's presence: God will dwell with humanity, and there will be a direct relationship between God and His people (Revelation 21:3).

No more suffering: There will be no more tears, mourning, or pain, as the old order of things will have passed away (Revelation 21:4).

Eternal life: Believers will experience eternal life in the presence of God, enjoying a life of worship, service, and fellowship with God and other believers (John 14:23).



The Spirit and the Bride

In Revelation 22:17, the Spirit and the Bride say, "Come!" inviting those who are thirsty to come and drink from the water of life. This invitation is A call to salvation: The Spirit and the Bride are inviting people to come to Jesus Christ and receive salvation (John 3:16).

A call to spiritual refreshment: The water of life symbolizes spiritual refreshment and nourishment, which believers can experience through a personal relationship with Jesus Christ (John 4:14).

Scriptural References:

Isaiah 65:17, “For behold , I create new heavens and a new earth, and the former things shall not be remembered or come into mind."

Revelation 21:1 "Then I saw a new heaven and a new earth, for the first heaven and the first earth had passed away, and the sea was no more."

Revelation 21:3 "And I heard a loud voice from the throne saying, 'Behold, the dwelling place of God is with man. He will dwell with them, and they will be his people, and God himself will be with them as their God.'"

Revelation 21:4 " He will wipe away every tear from their eyes, and death shall be no more, neither shall there be mourning nor crying nor pain anymore, for the former things have passed away."

John 14:23 " In my Father's house are many rooms. If it were not so, would I have told you that I go to prepare a place for you? And if I go and prepare a place for you, I will come again and will take you to myself, that where I am you may be also."

Revelation 22:17 " The Spirit and the Bride say, 'Come.' And let the one who hears say, 'Come.' And let the one who is thirsty come; let the one who desires take the water of life without price."

John 3:16 " For God so loved the world, that he gave his only Son, that whoever believes in him should not perish but have eternal life."

John 4:14 " But whoever drinks of the water that I will give him will never be thirsty again. The water that I will give him will become in him a spring of water welling up to eternal life."



Summation : The concept of "A New Heaven and Earth" and the role of "The Spirit and the Bride" highlight God's ultimate plan for humanity. The Spirit and the Bride invite people to come to Jesus Christ and experience salvation and spiritual refreshment. Believers can look forward to a future time when they will experience eternal life in the presence of God, free from sin and suffering.





THE GOSPEL OF BELIEVING IN JESUS CHRIST

The gospel is the good news of salvation through faith in Jesus Christ. It's a message of love, redemption, and forgiveness.

Key Focus :

Jesus is the Son of God: "In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God." (John 1:1)

Jesus died for our sins: "For God so loved the world that he gave his one and only Son, that whoever believes in him shall not perish but have eternal life." (John 3:16)

Jesus rose from the dead: "But God raised him from the dead, and for many days he appeared to those who had come up with him from Galilee to Jerusalem." (Acts 13:30-31)

Salvation through faith: "For it is by grace you have been saved, through faith—and this is not from yourselves, it is the gift of God—" (Ephesians 2:8)



Benefits of Believing in Jesus Christ:

Forgiveness of sins: "If we confess our sins, he is faithful and just and will forgive us our sins and purify us from all unrighteousness." (1 John 1:9)

Eternal life: "For God did not send his Son into the world to condemn the world, but to save the world through him." (John 3:17)

Peace with God: "Therefore, since we have been justified through faith, we have peace with God through our Lord Jesus Christ." (Romans 5:1)



Call to Action:

Believe in Jesus Christ: "That if you confess with your mouth, 'Jesus is Lord,' and believe in your heart that God raised him from the dead, you will be saved." (Romans 10:9)

Repent and turn to God: "Repent, then, and turn to God, so that your sins may be wiped out." (Acts 3:19)

By believing in Jesus Christ, you can experience the transformative power of the gospel and live a life filled with hope, joy, and purpose.

RECEIVE SALVATION: God Loves Us. God created us for fellowship and dearly desires for us to be restored to Him. Jesus Came to Give Life to Us. We can choose to receive God’s restoration and abundance of life through Christ Jesus.



SALVATION PRAYER AND BAPTISM IN THE HOLY SPIRIT

SALVATION PRAYER

"Dear Lord Jesus, I invite You into my heart today to be my Lord and Savior. Thank You for dying on the cross for my sins and forgiving me. I turn away from the devil's influence and surrender my life to You. Thank You, God, for loving me and saving me. From now on, I choose to live for You. Amen."

BAPTISM IN THE HOLY SPIRIT

"Dear Heavenly Father, I come to You in the name of Jesus. I believe Jesus is the Son of God, who died and was raised from the dead. I ask You to fill me with the Holy Spirit, with the evidence of speaking in tongues. I believe I receive the Holy Spirit as I pray, and I expect to manifest the fruit of the Spirit, including speaking in tongues, in Jesus' name. Amen."

These prayers are a personal expression of faith and commitment to God. May they guide you in your spiritual journey. THANK YOU!
